docs.draggable.component: `Draggable` marks an element a pointer may pick up — and says, as its ONE word of policy, where
the element goes when a drop is REFUSED: `onReject: "home"` flies it back to the seat it left,
`"stay"` strands it where the finger let go. That is the whole atom. It requires `Bounded`,
because a drag needs a footprint to hit-test and to carry.
```ts
import { node, Bounded, Surfaced, Transformable, Draggable, draggable, onRejectOf } from "game-kit"
const card = node("card",
Bounded({ bounds: rect(1, 1.4) }),
Surfaced({ surface: "queen" }),
Transformable({ at: { x: -1.2, y: 0 } }),
Draggable({ onReject: "home" }))
draggable(card)   // true — the pick's predicate
onRejectOf(card)  // "home" — what a refused drop does
## The atom is data; the drag is wiring
Nothing here moves by itself. A game wires the pointer to the motion runtime, and every piece of
that wiring is the kit's: `pick` reads the topmost draggable off the same plan the painter drew,
`grab` hands the run to the one clock, `dragTo` retargets the chase spring on every move — one
paint, never a tree write — and `release` hands the cards back.
```ts
const motion = attachMotion(host, painter)
view.addEventListener("pointerdown", (e) => {
const hit = pick(host, host.root, glassOf(view, e), draggable)
if (!hit) return
motion.grab([{ id: hit.id, offset: { x: 0, y: 0 } }],
{ anchor: originOf(hit) })   // the feel is the tuning's — patch a field here to differ per gesture
view.addEventListener("pointermove", (e) => motion.dragTo(toUnits(host, glassOf(view, e))))
view.addEventListener("pointerup", () => {
// ask the rules; on a refusal the atom answers: home — leave the tree alone and let the
// reconcile fly the card back; stay — write the release seat in as the new rest
motion.release(hit.id)
## Why `onReject` is the only field
Where a drop is ALLOWED is the zone's business (`Acceptor`), what leaves a pile is the pile's
(`Grabber`), and who may lift at all is the seat's (`Grippable`). What is left over — the one
question nobody else answers — is what a refusal does to the element itself. A trail (the ghost a
dragged card leaves behind) is deliberately NOT a field yet: it returns with the mechanism that
draws one.
## The feel is the runtime's
The lag behind the finger, the lean into motion and the lift pop are the spring carry —
`Engine/Motion` explains the clock, and the knobs on these scenes drive it live. The carry STYLE
is a registry name: `rigid` keeps a run one plank about the grab, `loose` turns each card in
place, and a game registers its own the way it registers a surface.
docs.draggable.drag: One card you can pick up — drag it with your own pointer — and one stone you cannot: the pick asks
`draggable`, and the stone never had the atom. Nothing in this scene accepts a drop, so every
release is a REFUSED one and `onReject` is the whole verdict: `home` flies the card back on the
spring, `stay` strands it where the finger let go, as its new rest.
`lift` and `lean` are the carry's feel: the pop while held, and how far the card banks into
horizontal motion. Both unwind to nothing at rest — the feel lives in flight, never in the tree.
docs.draggable.run: A column that travels as a RUN: grab any card and it leads every card below it — the same carry a
solitaire column rides. `carry` is the split the styles exist for: `rigid` co-rotates the whole
run about the grab point, one coherent plank; `loose` turns each card about its own middle, the
per-card look a horizontal hand wants. Set `lean` to zero and the two styles are the same picture
— the difference IS what a tilt does to the seats.
